name: AD843 (34 MHz CBFET JFET-input single op-amp)
tagline: ADI's 34 MHz, 250 V/us CBFET single op-amp. A DiyEden/Soomal headphone-amp study called it the only rival to the OPA627, and smoother; Head-Fi opinion is split.
technology: Fast-settling JFET-input single op-amp on ADI's CBFET process. The ADI data sheet is titled '34 MHz, CBFET Fast Settling Op Amp': 34 MHz bandwidth, 250 V/us slew rate, 135 ns settling to 0.01% for a 10 V step, 0.6 nA input bias current. ADI's SPICE macro-model (Rev. A, 1/92) uses a p-channel JFET input pair, with the dominant pole at about 1.23 kHz and about 10.7 mA typical supply current. Single channel only; ADI never made a dual AD843. Packages: 8-lead plastic DIP (N-8), 16-pin SOIC (R-16), cerdip (Q) and metal can (H).

lineage.period: c. 1990 onward (the macro-model is copyright 1991 and dated 1/92 Rev. A). Still in production: ADI's product page says at least one model is in production.
lineage.notes: The macro-model is credited 'JCB / PMI', i.e. modelled by ADI's Precision Monolithics group. No second sources or licensed copies were found. The discovery notes treat the AD843 as a separate die from the AD845 and AD847. The ADI product page says the part is appropriate for new designs but that newer alternatives may exist.

reputation.summary: A niche cult part with split opinion. DiyEden published a Chinese translation of an English headphone-amp op-amp study on Soomal (2005). It quotes an article called 'The best op-amp I've heard' naming the AD843 the only op-amp that can rival the OPA627. The author found it smoother than the OPA627, trading some resolution for smoothness, with 'boldness, charm, vitality and passion'. A pair cost about half as much as a pair of OPA627s. The same study rates the AD845 as less detailed and says to upgrade to the AD843, and rates the AD8610 as having more detail and smoothness than the AD843. Head-Fi opinion (from an earlier search summary, not re-checked) is largely negative: 'harsh and unpleasant', 'no competition for OPA637', 'stay away from this - bad offset, oscillation, etc.'. One user found 2x AD843JN on an adapter 'really good' but warm, because of the high quiescent current. It also appears in Maverick TubeMagic D1 op-amp rolling lists. No objective measurements (Audio Science Review, Samuel Groner) were found.
sonic_descriptors: bold / energetic ('气魄、神韵、活力和热情')
typical_uses: headphone amplifier op-amp rolling (CMoy-style, single-channel sockets)
DAC output stage rolling, used in pairs on dual adapters
replacement for OPA627 in single sockets
caveats: High quiescent current: 13 mA max per the data sheet, about 10.7 mA typical in ADI's model. It runs warm and is poor for battery amps.
Needs a high supply voltage: hobbyist-measured minimums of 8.2 V and 12.2 V. The sound degrades quickly as the supply voltage drops.
Head-Fi reports of bad offset and oscillation. It is a 34 MHz, 250 V/us part, so it is sensitive to layout and decoupling.
Single only: dual-socket use needs two chips on an adapter.
The surface-mount version is a 16-pin SOIC (R-16), not an SO-8, so it does not fit standard SO-8 adapters.

counterfeit_notes: No reports of fake AD843s were found, but this was not searched specifically. Generic caution: DIP AD843JN/KN parts sold on marketplaces are likely relabelled or pulled parts. Check the ADI logo style and date code. Measure quiescent current: roughly 10-13 mA is expected (13 mA data-sheet max, about 10.7 mA model typical). A much lower Iq points to a substituted die such as a TL071-class part. Also check the offset against the grade limits: 2 mV for J, 1 mV for K. A genuine SOIC part is a 16-pin R-16 package; an 8-pin SOIC marked AD843 is suspect.
alternatives: OPA627 / OPA827 (TI JFET-input; the reference it is compared with in the DiyEden study)
AD8610 / AD8620 (ADI precision JFET; DiyEden rates it smoother, with more detail than the AD843, and much lower supply current)
AD845 (ADI JFET-input sibling; cheaper, smoother, less detailed per DiyEden)
ADA4627-1 (modern ADI OPA627-class JFET single; suggested successor, not compared by listeners)
OPA828 (modern TI high-speed JFET single; suggested successor)

claims_confirmed: The ADI data sheet title is '34 MHz, CBFET Fast Settling Op Amp' and the current revision is Rev. D (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/AD843.pdf)
The data sheet specifies 34 MHz bandwidth, 135 ns settling to 0.01% for a 10 V step and 0.6 nA input bias current (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/AD843.pdf)
There are five grades: J/K 0 to +70 C, A/B -40 to +85 C, S -55 to +125 C (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/AD843.pdf)
The connection diagrams show a 16-pin SOIC (R-16) and an 8-lead plastic DIP (N-8) (https://www.analog.com/static/imported-files/data_sheets/AD843.pdf)
The AD843 family is in Production; AD843KNZ, AD843JRZ-16-REEL7, AD843SQ and AD843SQ/883B are listed as Production (https://analog.com/en/products/ad843.html)
Input voltage noise is 19 nV/rtHz and supply current is 13 mA max, per a search summary (https://datasheet.octopart.com/AD843KN-Analog-Devices-datasheet-7595.pdf)

Distributor and third-party data-sheet copies exist (https://www.digikey.com/htmldatasheets/production/51948/0/0/1/ad843.html, https://www.alldatasheet.com/datasheet-pdf/pdf/48472/AD/AD843KN.html, https://www.datasheetcatalog.com/datasheets_pdf/A/D/8/4/AD843.shtml)

revision_chain_notes: Only one vendor document exists: the Analog Devices AD843 data sheet, titled "34 MHz, CBFET Fast Settling Op Amp". The AD843 was ADI-only. No second source, licensee or acquirer re-issue was found; the Precision Monolithics group was in-house at ADI. Chain, oldest to newest: the original edition (Rev. 0 in ADI's current scheme, or an unlettered data-book edition) is MISSING. It is c. 1990; the SPICE macro-model is copyright 1991 and dated 1/92 Rev. A, but that date belongs to the model, not the data sheet. Rev. A, Rev. B and Rev. C are also MISSING: no copy or date was found by letter in 4 searches, and no search summary showed a "REV. x" footer or a revision history block for the AD843. The only confirmed revision is Rev. D, the current one on analog.com/media/.../AD843.pdf (13 pages, about 485 KB) and on RadioLocman; its date and change log were still not shown. New copies found, all with revision not shown: Farnell 2147042.pdf, alldatasheet 1011842, Datasheet Archive's index page, Futurlec's AD843JN page and datasheetq/en. Which letter a copy holds can only be read from the file itself. Old alldatasheet IDs (48465 and 48472), datasheetcatalog, digchip, Datasheet Archive and Futurlec are the likeliest to hold pre-D editions. That is inferred from their IDs, which suggest early uploads, and is unconfirmed. Next steps: check Wayback captures of the archive seed URLs, the old analog.com static/imported-files path, for earlier letters. Also check the ADI 1990/1992 Linear Products Data Book scans on bitsavers or worldradiohistory for the original edition. The legacy ADI path pattern www.analog.com/UploadedFiles/Data_Sheets/ is another option, but it was NOT confirmed for the AD843 and is not listed as a seed.
